title: bug: a worktree completion whose push origin applied but answered [remote rejected] still loses its receipt journal when the one re-check fetch also fails, so the retry records plain nothing-to-commit and QA's landed gate parks the row BLOCKED again (residual of task-bc6ba91b, both launchers)
description:
Residual of task-bc6ba91b (named in its plan's approachesConsidered #3; that DoD kept this path exactly as before). After task-bc6ba91b, a `![remote rejected]` push gets one re-check fetch (wt_remote_holds / Test-MoeRemoteHolds). When all 3 land_fetch tries of that re-check fail while origin really holds C, wt_publish still runs `rm -f` on the receipt journal (moe-agent.sh ~:7530; ps1 Publish-MoeWorktreeLanding ~:7144 Remove-Item) and routes MOE_PUSH_FAILED unlanded remote. The retry's L5 then finds the merged tree equal to origin's target, but with no journal the $jc recovery (sh ~:7600, LAND_WT_RECOVERED) cannot owe the completion row, so it records plain MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and qa_landed_gate blocks: the task-7cef0861 incident loop, only rarer.
Repro: the postflight-worktree.cjs case wt-remote-rejected, arm fetch-fails (WT_GIT_PUSH_REMOTE_REJECTED + WT_GIT_FETCH_FAIL_AFTER_PUSH), followed by a LANDING-RETRY completion with fetch restored.
Direction (the planner decides): when the re-check could not run (fetch failed), keep the journal (for example 'push remote-rejected-unverified: …'), so the retry's L5 or a pre-flight replay (reconcile_push) can still prove C and owe the row; a re-check that proves C absent still deletes it.
definitionOfDone: In both launchers, a [remote rejected] push whose re-check fetch fails keeps a receipt journal naming C, while still routing MOE_PUSH_FAILED unlanded remote with the rescue ref as today.

The landing retry of such a task, once origin's target is fetchable and holds C, records the owed completion row (pushed:true) and a landed finalize instead of a plain MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT; a re-check that proves C absent still removes the journal.
The worktree landing harness covers both launchers; parity-check.{sh,ps1} and worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} pass; scripts/CLAUDE.md and the design doc's L9 text describe the kept journal.

implementationPlan.description:
The sh wrapper, scripts/moe-agent.sh (line numbers at d1062cb0). Touch only these functions; the VM-route blocks belong to open rows cc4213c0 (sh), 62ec51f1 and d861f3de (ps1). Edit in place with a TOOL-witnessed editor, never temp+mv, then run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`.

1. wt_remote_holds (:7487) becomes tri-state:
   - 0: origin's TARGET holds C;
   - 1: the fetch worked and origin lacks C (merge-base exit 1);
   - 2: unverifiable.
   For 2, set LAND_RECHECK_DETAIL: "git fetch failed: $LAND_FETCH_ERR" when land_fetch fails, or "git merge-base --is-ancestor exited $rc" for any other exit. It still never pushes.

2. wt_push_target (:7500):
   - Set LAND_PUSH_UNVERIFIED="" on entry.
   - In the rc-2 branch, a 0 keeps today's APPLIED line and rc=0.
   - A 2 sets LAND_PUSH_UNVERIFIED=true and appends "; the re-check could not read origin's $1 ($LAND_RECHECK_DETAIL)" to LAND_PUSH_DETAIL.
   - rc stays 2 for both 1 and 2, so run_migration_landing's `2)` arm is unchanged; it has no journal and only prints the richer detail.

3. A new helper `wt_journal_unverified JOURNAL`: 0 when the journal's pushResult starts with the prefix (one python read; 1 on any failure).

4. wt_publish (:7520), the rc-2 arm:
   - When LAND_PUSH_UNVERIFIED=true, keep the journal and set its pushResult with `wt_journal_push_result "$1" "push remote-rejected-unverified: $LAND_PUSH_DETAIL"`;
   - else `rm -f "$1"` as today.
   - LAND_CODE=MOE_PUSH_FAILED and LAND_MESSAGE are unchanged, so the unlanded remote route, the rescue ref and the failed row are as today (DoD 1).

5. wt_land_rounds' journal check (:7571-7581). For jw=remote with an unverified journal, run wt_remote_holds "${jt#refs/heads/}" "$ja":
   - 0: jc="$ja" plus wt_journal_push_result "$journal" "pushed $ja to origin/${jt#refs/heads/}". L5 then takes the existing $jc path: LAND_WT_RECOVERED, then wt_land_published sends the row (pushed:true, from the 'pushed ' prefix) and finalizes landed (DoD 2).
   - 1: rm -f the journal, which the fresh round supersedes.
   - 2: refuse with LAND_OUTCOME=refused, MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_UNRECONCILED_INTENT and "receipt journal $journal holds a [remote rejected] push of $ja that no re-check could verify ($LAND_RECHECK_DETAIL)".
   Every other journal takes the existing receipt_landed_as logic, unchanged; put it in an else.

6. receipt_replay (:6550): add a block BEFORE the existing `[ "$wt" = remote ]` reconcile_push block, for wt=remote with an unverified journal. A [remote rejected] C is never re-pushed; a fetch decides.
   - rc 2: the still-unverified WARN, then continue.
   - Compute phase=moe_pinned_attempt_phase "$aid" "$tid" "$gen" "$owner".
   - rc 0 with phase not finalizing: the holds-C line, then continue. The journal stays for step 5.
   - Before any drop or overwrite, re-read and compare (`[ "$(receipt_journal_fields "$f")" != "$fields" ]`, then the existing 'rewritten or removed meanwhile' line), per mem:gotcha-worktree-receipt-replay-race: a worktree journal has no live marker.
   - rc 1: with phase finalizing, first replay_unlanded ... remote MOE_PUSH_FAILED "origin's <T> does not hold the [remote rejected] landing $after"; if that fails, keep the journal. Then rm, print the does-not-hold line, and continue.
   - rc 0 with phase finalizing: wt_journal_push_result "$f" "pushed $after to origin/<T>", then fall through. The existing block reconciles (its fetch finds C, so there is no push), records the row pushed:true, finalizes landed and drops the journal.

7. Fix the header comments of wt_remote_holds, wt_push_target, wt_publish, wt_land_rounds and receipt_replay.

Error handling: only ENOENT-free proof moves anything. A failed fetch never drops, marks or settles a journal, and no path re-pushes after [remote rejected].
implementationPlan.note:
sh changes:
- wt_remote_holds is tri-state (0 held, 1 absent, 2 unverifiable) and sets LAND_RECHECK_DETAIL.
- wt_push_target sets LAND_PUSH_UNVERIFIED and appends the re-check detail suffix. It still returns rc 2, so migration is unchanged.
- New wt_journal_unverified helper.
- wt_publish rc 2 marks the journal `push remote-rejected-unverified: …`. Beyond the plan, it then runs `wt_journal_unverified || rm -f`: an unmarked journal (C absent, or a failed best-effort mark) is dropped as before rather than left as a plain journal that a replay's reconcile_push would re-push.
- wt_land_rounds: an unverified remote journal is proven by fetch. Held: jc=C, marked 'pushed …', then the existing LAND_WT_RECOVERED path. Absent: rm. Unverifiable: refused UNRECONCILED_INTENT. Every other journal goes through the existing receipt_landed_as path.
- receipt_replay gets a pre-block. Unverifiable keeps the journal with a WARN. Held and not finalizing keeps it, with the holds-C line. Held and finalizing marks it 'pushed' and falls through to reconcile_push, which does not push. Absent routes a finalizing attempt through replay_unlanded first, then drops the journal. Every drop or mark re-reads and compares first.
- Header comments updated.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Both launchers. A worktree completion push answered `[remote rejected]` keeps its one re-check fetch. When that fetch fails, the receipt journal is now KEPT, its pushResult marked `push remote-rejected-unverified: <detail>`, while the landing still routes MOE_PUSH_FAILED, unlanded remote, with the rescue ref and the failed row as today. That journal is settled only by a fetch of origin, never a re-push. The task's next landing (L5) proves it: origin holding C makes C that landing's, recorded with the owed completion row (pushed:true) and a landed finalize instead of a plain MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT; origin lacking C drops the journal and the fresh round lands; an unverifiable fetch refuses MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_UNRECONCILED_INTENT. A pre-flight replay uses the same fetch-only proof: absent drops the journal (after routing a still-finalizing attempt unlanded); held keeps it for the task's next landing, or settles it at once (row, landed finalize, drop) while its attempt is still finalizing; an unverifiable fetch keeps it. A re-check that proves C absent at push time still deletes the journal.
acceptanceCriteria: sh and ps1: the wt-remote-rejected fetch-fails arm keeps the journal, its pushResult starting `push remote-rejected-unverified: `, and still routes MOE_PUSH_FAILED, unlanded remote, with a rescue ref at T and landingRetry count 1.

Its retry, with fetch restored, logs the replay's holds-C keep line, then lands with finalize [['landed',C]], the row ['committed',C,pushed:true], the journal gone and landingRetry null. Its log has no MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and origin is pushed nothing new.
The new 'absent' arm (a pre-receive refusal and a failed re-check fetch): the journal is kept, then the retry's replay drops it and a fresh C2 lands, finalized landed and pushed:true.
wtUnlanded's 'rejected' arm (a working re-check proves C absent) leaves no journal.
parity-check.{sh,ps1}, postflight-migration.cjs and the held-out worktree-landing.{sh,ps1} pass unchanged.
scripts/CLAUDE.md (the L9-L10 and Replay bullets) and the design doc's L9 row, §2.9 and L9 summary describe the kept journal.
invariants: After a [remote rejected] answer: never a re-push, a force flag or a new round, at push time, in the replay or at L5.
Only a successful fetch proving ancestry turns an unverified journal into a landing. Only a successful fetch proving absence drops it.
Every replay drop or overwrite of a journal re-reads and compares it first (worktree journals have no live marker).
'push unknown' journals, the [rejected], applied and reconcile_push paths, and migration's outcomes keep their behavior.
Shared strings and the pushResult prefix are byte-identical in both wrappers; the ps1 UTF-8 BOM is kept.
compatibility: A journal written by either wrapper is replayed or landed correctly by the other (the same JSON keys and prefix).
Journals without the prefix (older wrappers, 'push unknown', 'pushed') take exactly today's paths.
No daemon, MCP tool or .moe/ schema change. pushResult is a local journal field.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Keep the journal and change nothing else: rejected. The unchanged replay would reconcile_push it, re-pushing a [remote rejected] C while origin is at B. When origin holds C, it records the row without pushed and drops the journal, so the retry ends in a plain MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT, against DoD 2.
2. Have the replay settle every unverified journal (row, then drop): rejected for the same reason. The retry's L5 then has no journal, so it cannot finalize landed. Worktree journals have no live marker, and every seat's poll replays them, so the replay would always win that race.
3. Chosen: the fetch-only proof in three places. At push time a failed fetch keeps the journal. At L5 the next landing proves it and recovers C (row pushed:true, landed finalize) or drops it. The replay proves it too: absent drops it, held keeps it for the landing (or settles it at once while still finalizing), and unverifiable keeps it.
4. A new wt_push_target return code for unverified: rejected. run_migration_landing's case would send it into the 'rebuilding' arm. A LAND_PUSH_UNVERIFIED flag keeps rc 2.
5. Recording the owed row in the replay while keeping the journal: rejected. It re-sends on every poll of every seat, the spam that mem:decision-receipt-replay-owed-ledger-and-any-seat-finalize rejected.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The harness's landRun is a full wrapper iteration. The retry's order is: pre-flight claim, receipt_replay, worktree_resume (merging origin's C into W gives LANDING-RETRY: remote), the CLI, the completion, L2 (which commits the merge [T, C]), L5 (merge-tree(C, T') equals C's tree), then $jc recovery.
- moe_pinned_attempt_phase is a disk read. The harness's launch() wipes .moe/attempts, so a retry reads the old attempt as 'mismatch' (not finalizing), as production's closed attempt does.
- receipt_ledger_send re-reads the journal file. ps1's replay uses the parsed object, while Complete-MoeWorktreeLanding re-reads it.
- worktree-landing remoteRejected uses a pre-receive refusal with a working fetch, so it stays on the absent path (one push, MOE_PUSH_FAILED).
- postflight-migration's 'remote-rejected' asserts only MOE_PUSH_FAILED appears in the log.
planningNotes.risks:
- Open rows share the wrappers. cc4213c0 (REVIEW) holds the sh VM route; 62ec51f1 (WORKING) and d861f3de (BLOCKED) hold the ps1 VM route. Touch only the named functions, since adjacent-line edits conflict under merge-tree (mem:gotcha-adjacent-line-edits-conflict-in-worktree-landing).
- Peer replays can race a live lander's journal. Guard every replay drop and mark, and accept that a peer may record the row first (the daemon merges a repeated sha).
- A best-effort pushResult write that fails leaves a plain L8 journal, which takes today's unknown-outcome path. That is acceptable and needs no extra code.
- The gate takes about 17-20 min and needs a detached run plus polling. The Windows legs need /mnt/d and the env -u prefix.
- Held unverified journals print one replay line per poll until the task lands again, as the existing kept-journal lines do.

completionSummary:
Both launchers. A worktree completion push answered [remote rejected] still gets ONE re-check fetch. The re-check (wt_remote_holds / Test-MoeRemoteHolds) is now tri-state:
- 0: origin holds C;
- 1: the fetch worked and origin lacks C;
- 2: unverifiable, with the reason in LAND_RECHECK_DETAIL / $script:MoeRecheckDetail.

On 2, wt_publish / Publish-MoeWorktreeLanding KEEPS the receipt journal as `push remote-rejected-unverified: <detail>`, and the push detail gains "; the re-check could not read origin's <T> (...)". The route is unchanged: MOE_PUSH_FAILED, unlanded remote, the rescue ref, the failed row and landingRetry. A re-check that proves C absent still drops the journal.

A kept journal is settled only by a fetch, never a re-push.
- The task's next landing (L5, wt_land_rounds / Invoke-MoeWorktreeRounds):
  - held: C becomes this landing's (LAND_WT_RECOVERED), with the owed row pushed:true and a landed finalize instead of a plain MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT;
  - absent: the journal is dropped and a fresh C lands;
  - unverifiable: refused MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_UNRECONCILED_INTENT.
- The pre-flight replay:
  - absent: the journal is dropped, after routing a still-finalizing attempt unlanded;
  - held: the journal is kept for the next landing, or settled at once while its attempt is finalizing (ps1 also updates the in-memory pushResult);
  - unverifiable: the journal is kept.
  - Every drop or mark re-reads and compares the journal first.

Shared strings are byte-identical in both wrappers. The ps1 BOM is kept, and migration is unchanged (rc 2 kept).

Harness (postflight-worktree.cjs):
- The fetch-fails arm now asserts the kept journal. Its retry lands with finalize [['landed',C]] and the row ['committed',C,pushed:true], with no NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and no new push.
- A new 'absent' arm: the replay drops C1 and a fresh C2 lands.
- wtUnlanded 'rejected' asserts the journal is gone.
